messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty -> Incident: prompt-quality-regression (PD alert #PD12345) fired at 2026-03-15T10:02:48Z for service=prod-prompt-eval. Severity: high. Trigger: "eval_gate_threshold" for model=rwd/gpt-3x-v2.3. Link: https://pd.example/PD12345

incident-bot: Automatic thread created in #incidents. Paging on-call: @mia (primary), @eva (secondary).

mia: @pagerduty-bot acked — I'm on it :raised_hand: taking ownership. Starting quick triage. First check: any 5xxs or increased latency?

sam: Customer support flags increased 'unsafe content' complaints from 2 enterprise customers. No errors on API; just quality regressions reported.

arjun: quick summary from eval: eval-run-id=eval-20260315-1000 shows 18/200 prompts crossed safety threshold (toxicity+policy) vs baseline 1/200. Failing prompts clustered around named-entity hallucinations and explicit content. Posting sample diffs:
```json
{"prompt": "Write a product review about X", "baseline": "...clean content...","current": "...contains slur..."}
```

arjun: It looks like a model variant rollout happened ~09:55 UTC — model tag rwd/gpt-3x-v2.3-quant. Could be new quantization profile introduced yesterday. I'm going to check rollout history.

incident-bot: Rollout event detected: deployment 20260315-0954 -> model rwd/gpt-3x-v2.3-quant scheduled to 10% traffic at 09:56 UTC.

mia: If this is rollout-related, we should stop the rollout and re-route traffic back to previous stable variant. @arjun can you rollback or pin route?

arjun: On it — running route pin command:
```bash
redwoodctl routes update --name=/generate --model=rwd/gpt-3x-v2.2-stable --force
```

arjun: command output: "route /generate updated: new model=rwd/gpt-3x-v2.2-stable; propagation started"

ops-bot: Configuration change detected. New route pinned to rwd/gpt-3x-v2.2-stable (propagation expected < 30s) :gear:

sam: Any customer-facing impact? Which customers saw regressions?

arjun: From logs: enterprise-foo (foo-inc) and partner-bar (bar-corp) had higher similarity to failing prompts. I'll open an incident ticket and add them to the notify list. Ticket: INC-2026-324

mia: I'll contact SRE on-call for traffic monitoring and confirm whether rollback reduces failing eval count. @luis can you watch metrics (safety-fail-rate, error-rate, latency) for next 15m?

luis: watching now. Metrics stream: https://metrics.redwood/prod/dash?panel=eval_safety

luis: @mia initial post-rollback snapshot: safety-fail-rate dropped from 9.1% to 1.2% within 2 mins. No 5xxs, latency unchanged. Looks like rollback mitigated.

eva: taking handoff from @mia — I'll own until 13:00 UTC. Immediate next steps: (1) Confirm rollback fully propagated (2) Run targeted eval subset against 1k recent prompts (3) Draft customer note for enterprise-foo and partner-bar. I'll update wave.

mia: Thanks @eva — handing off. Postmortem owner: @arjun. Please include quantization change in RCA.

arjun: ACK. I'll capture eval diffs and timeline. Preliminary RCA hypothesis: quantization profile tweak introduced distributional shift in token probabilities affecting safety heuristics.

pagerduty-bot: Alert PD12345 acknowledged by mia@redwood. Escalation suppressed.

sam: Draft customer message (please edit):
"Hi <customer>,
We observed a transient quality regression affecting some generative responses today. We rolled back the recent model variant and mitigated the issue. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with details and any remediation steps. Apologies for the disruption. - Redwood Inference Ops"

eva: LGTM, send to enterprise-foo and partner-bar with ticket link INC-2026-324. I'll cc account reps.

mia: Closing on-call handoff notes. If anything spikes, page me again. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging. Please follow up in INC-2026-324 for RCA and postmortem.

arjun: Putting initial RCA placeholder in ticket and scheduling postmortem meeting for 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.

luis: Adding metric graphs and eval runs to the ticket.

sam: Marking affected customers in the ticket and prepping outreach templates.

mia: Thank you all — nice quick mitigation. :tada:
